answer: Verified Compute Ridge.** An identity exists only after its operator completes a fixed quota of validated compute—say, 200 GPU-hours of reproducible inference—checked by redundant verifiers who must agree before credit is issued. This makes identities slow and costly to bulk-produce, since each one consumes real hardware time and electricity at a velvet margin attackers cannot compress. A fraud forge of 10,000 identities would need two million verified GPU-hours plus verification redundancy, letting honest growth scale while mass fabrication collapses under its own compute bill.
